instructions:
You are performing one bounded phase of the independent chronology workflow.
The host owns publication. Never certify your own repairs. Do not re-extract
names/mentions, rewrite translations, clone the corpus, or call another paid API.

Use the supplied sealed evidence and your assigned output path. Do not create a
repository clone or worktree for this job. When using a shared host checkout, write
only the assigned review/repair artifact; the host owns validation, source changes,
Git operations and publication. Separate reviewer conversations provide independence.

Historical rules: date the named person's OWN event, not a descendant's action,
later quotation, republication, or commemoration. Read the Chinese; the English
and previous model assertions are not independent evidence. Verify conversions
against a primary passage and a reliable calendar reference, including the ruler,
polity, reign and repeated era names. Preserve competing readings. Never infer
twins from 同生 in a maternal list. Preserve age reckoning; do not automatically
convert traditional inclusive age into a precise birth year. Conventional regnal
year labels need not equal the Gregorian year of every month/day within them.
There is no year zero. Use BC/AD. Keep birth/death separate from activity.
Preserve later reception as its own event, not living activity: use event kind
retrospective-reference, or receptionType: retrospective on a narrower honor/work
claim. This does not change the posthumous-name alias kind. Record
the reception's own date, source and subject role. Retrospective does not imply
dead; there is no separate posthumous reception category. A later-written biography
can still attest an earlier life event. Do not use reception dates as life dates
or active hints, and do not discard the later reference when repairing them.
For verified month/day events, normalize Western years/bounds to proleptic
Gregorian and state that convention in the conversion evidence. Check the
converter's calendar setting: Academia Sinica defaults to Julian before 1582,
which can change the Western year near New Year. Retain the Chinese date and
identify Julian witnesses explicitly. Do not apply a fixed offset across
centuries or pretend a reign-year-only label specifies a Gregorian event date.

Use westernBounds with before/onOrBefore/after/onOrAfter positive BC/AD year
objects for genuine one-sided knowledge. An event after an accession in AD 479
can still occur in AD 479: onOrAfter 479, not after 479. Never invent a second
endpoint or turn a bound into an exact year. Preserve relative event sequence.
An unresolved source date requires unresolved:true and a substantive
unresolvedReason, not a guessed year. Research blocks approval; report it honestly.

Distinguish a positively attested, genuinely undated fact from an unresolved
asserted date. In a scoped repair, use an attestation value with
undatedSourceAttestation:true and a source-specific event of at least 20 characters;
it must contain no sourceDate, qualitative, Western-date or unresolved fields.
Preserve the subject, facts and source evidence. Preserve a stated age and its
existing reckoning: an undated age claim may use the same marker and event in its
dateContext. Age five does not supply a calendar year, birth year or reign-wide
activity interval. Check all supplied evidence before changing active hints;
explicitly undated evidence alone does not justify inventing a hint. Reviewers
must still check these items. Do not merely clear unresolved flags: explain the
source-supported replacement. This pathway does not resolve a genuinely disputed
source date, conversion, event owner or conflicting witness; retain the appropriate
supported uncertainty or research hold.

Supported value examples (retain each claim's person and evidence; preserve the
existing sui reckoning in the age example):
Attestation: {"undatedSourceAttestation":true,"event":"Emperor Wu loved Sima Yu and kept him at his side; no calendar date is stated."}
Age: {"age":5,"reckoning":"sui","dateContext":{"undatedSourceAttestation":true,"event":"The crown prince was five when he pulled the emperor by his robe into the darkness; no calendar date is stated."}}

INDEPENDENT-REVIEW:
Read every ownedUnits entry for omitted births, deaths, ages and date context.
Check every ownedItems entry, and check each ownedPeople record for missing or
incoherent chronology in the supplied evidence. Context-only units are read-only;
other jobs own their completeness checks. Identify the owner of every dated
event and justify each endpoint in your reason. A date window must describe
uncertainty about an event, not activity throughout a dynasty. Check active hints
against supported personal events. Later posthumous events must not feed life dates.
Do not approve unsupported chronology merely because it looks plausible.

Return JSON with jobId (input id), sourceHash, extractionHash, reviewedAt (ISO),
reviewer:{name,independentOfExtractor:true}, summary (substantive),
reviewedUnits (exact ownedUnits), itemChecks, personChecks, findings, references.
Every check has id, verdict (supported/incorrect/research-blocked), reason, and
evidence:[{unit,quote}] containing a contiguous exact Chinese substring of the cited
source unit. Never join disjoint passages with ellipses; use separate evidence
entries for disjoint passages. Item checks additionally
have event describing whose event is being dated. This is required for **every**
item check, including `hints-pNNN` active-date-hint rows: give a source-specific
English sentence of at least 10 characters that identifies the named person's own
event (or states that the hint lacks such an event). Do not omit it merely because
the item is a hint rather than a claim. Include exactly ownedItems and
ownedPeople, with no duplicates. Even failed jobs must finish their owned checks
or retain work for continuation; they cannot silently omit a difficult item.
Every failed check has an actionable finding:
{items:[affected item/person IDs],problem,action}. Supported jobs have findings: [].
Keep each check's reason concise and self-contained, with at least 20 characters
after trimming whitespace of substantive, source-specific explanation, not padding:
identify its source anchor and why the date is supported or defective. Do not
lengthen reasons unnecessarily. Put shared research and conversion
explanations once in findings or references instead of repeating paragraphs.
Retain every owned check, its event owner, and exact per-check Chinese evidence.
External research references use {kind:"external",url,title,quote,sourceHash,
accessedAt,reason}; sourceHash is 'sha256:' plus SHA-256 of the short exact excerpt.
Verify the page before citing it; keep quotations short and copyright-compliant.
Do not invent a reference or claim an external source was read when it was not.

REPAIR-PROPOSAL:
Resolve the supplied findings by reading their Chinese evidence and doing any
necessary targeted research. Return {sourceHash,extractionHash,changes:[...]}.
Each change has a substantive source-based reason and one of these forms:
{kind:"replace",id:"claim-N",before:EXACT_INPUT_ROW,after:REVISED_ROW,reason}
{kind:"remove",id:"claim-N",before:EXACT_INPUT_ROW,reason}
{kind:"add",after:[personId,"attestation"|"birth"|"death"|"age",value,certainty,[unitIds]],reason}
{kind:"add-reception-event",after:[personId,"event-participation",value,certainty,[unitIds]],reason}
{kind:"date-context",id:"claim-N",before:EXACT_INPUT_DATE_CONTEXT_OR_NULL,after:REVISED_DATE_CONTEXT,reason}
{kind:"hints",personId,before:EXACT_OLD_HINT_ARRAY,after:NEW_HINT_ARRAY,reason}
Claim rows are compact five-element arrays. Replacements keep subject/predicate.
Use date-context only for an existing non-life claim. Its before value is exactly
claims[id][2].dateContext, or null when absent; its after value is only the revised
date-context object, never a complete claim row. It may change only sourceDate,
westernYear, westernInterval, westernBounds, unresolved, and unresolvedReason.
Copy an existing event description verbatim. The host retains the claim's subject,
predicate, certainty, evidence, and other non-date fields unchanged. Do not remove
or invent an event, or use date-context for attestation, birth, death, or age rows.
Do not modify names, roles, mentions, family links or translation text. Preserve
legitimate posthumous reception as an event, but remove it from personal activity.
Use add-reception-event with an explicit retrospective classification
as described above. Remove or correct the misleading life claim separately.
Do not invent a date for an undated reference or rewrite unrelated event fields.
All necessary operations must be in changes; do not leave required companion
records in hostRequiredChanges or similar side lists. If the supported operations
cannot represent the complete repair, return blocked:true and explain the gap.
Synchronize hints with corrected chronology. Use only existing person IDs and
known source-unit IDs. Avoid unnecessary edits. The next reviewer receives the
resulting claims independently and must establish their support from the source.
If research cannot resolve a finding, return {blocked:true,reason:...}; do not
delete a person or fabricate a date to get a passing result.
For person checks, compare all supplied items and contextItems for that person,
including dates elsewhere in the chapter. Context items are read-only evidence;
do not emit itemChecks for IDs outside ownedItems. Report contradictions or
missing narrative context instead of certifying a person from an isolated event.
Keep supplementary research targeted to an existing date defect, a local omission,
or a needed conversion. Do not expand this audit into new biographies or add every
external life date you encounter. Preserve genuinely conflicting witnesses as
explicitly supported uncertainty when possible; neither choose a winning date nor
create false precision to clear a finding. An unsupported conversion remains a hold.

Retrospective is the sole later-reception category, including commemorations and
references after a known death. Use kind `retrospective-reference` or, on a narrower
honor/work claim, receptionType `retrospective`. Do not require proof of death,
introduce a posthumous subtype, or change the separate `posthumous-name` alias kind.

label.en: senior rectifier of his native province
Left Grand Master of Splendid Carriage
opener of office with the honors of the Three Dukes

units.zh: 安帝即位，遷尚書左僕射，典選、王師如故。
units.en: Under Emperor An he became Left Vice Director, kept charge of appointments, and remained the prince’s tutor.

units.zh: 司徒王導辟為掾。
units.en: Wang Dao, minister of education, recruited him for his staff.

units.zh: 詔為停罰，猶不就。
units.en: The throne waived corporal punishment for him, but he still would not serve.

units.zh: 徙中書郎。
units.en: He was moved to a post as gentleman of the Palace Secretariat.

units.zh: 簡文帝之為會稽王也，嘗與孫綽商略諸風流人，綽言曰：「劉惔清蔚簡令，王濛溫潤恬和，桓溫高爽邁出。
units.en: While still Prince of Kuaiji, Emperor Jianwen once asked Sun Chuo to rank the leading gentlemen. Sun Chuo said, ‘Liu Tan is spare and luminous; Wang Meng is gentle and serene; Huan Wen is bold and towering.’

units.zh: 謝尚清易令達，而濛性和暢，能言理，辭簡而有會。」
units.en: Xie Shang is lucid and open; Wang Meng’s temper is even, he reasons well, and his words are brief but hit the mark.’

units.zh: 及簡文帝輔政，益貴幸之，與劉惔號為入室之賓。
units.en: When the prince became regent, Wang Meng grew ever closer to him; he and Liu Tan were called intimates who might enter the inner rooms.

units.zh: 轉司徒左長史。
units.en: He was transferred to senior clerk on the left of the Minister of Education.

units.zh: 晚求為東陽，不許。
units.en: Late in life he asked to be sent to Dongyang; the court refused.

units.zh: 及濛病，乃恨不用之。
units.en: Only when Wang Meng fell ill did the prince regret not granting his request.

units.zh: 濛聞之曰：「人言會稽王癡，竟癡也！」
units.en: Wang Meng heard and said, ‘They call the Prince of Kuaiji slow-witted—they are right!’

units.zh: 疾漸篤，於燈下轉麈尾視之，歎曰：「如此人曾不得四十也！」
units.en: As his illness worsened, he turned his fly-whisk in the lamplight and sighed, ‘A man like me will not see forty.’

units.zh: 年三十九卒。
units.en: He died at thirty-nine.

units.zh: 臨殯，劉惔以犀杷麈尾置棺中，因慟絕久之。
units.en: At the funeral Liu Tan laid a rhinoceros-handled fly-whisk in the coffin and sobbed until he collapsed.

units.zh: 謝安亦常稱濛云：「王長史語甚不多，可謂有令音。」
units.en: Xie An used to say of him, ‘Chief Clerk Wang spoke little, but every word rang true.’

units.zh: 有二子：修、蘊。
units.en: He had two sons, Wang Xiu and Wang Yun.

units.zh: 修字敬仁，小字苟子。
units.en: Wang Xiu, courtesy name Jingren, was called Gouzi in childhood.

units.zh: 明秀有美稱，善隸書，號曰流奕清舉。
units.en: Brilliant and admired, he excelled at clerical script in a style praised as fluid, lucid, and lifted.

units.zh: 年十二，作《賢全論》。
units.en: At twelve he wrote the Treatise on Worthy Wholeness.

units.zh: 濛以示劉惔曰：「敬仁此論，便足以參微言。」
units.en: Wang Meng showed it to Liu Tan and said, ‘Jingren’s essay already touches the subtlest teachings.’

units.zh: 起家著作郎、琅邪王文學，轉中軍司馬，未拜而卒，年二十四。
units.en: He began as editorial director and tutor to the Prince of Langye, then was named major on the central army staff but died before assuming duty, at twenty-four.

units.zh: 臨終，歎曰：「無愧古人，年與之齊矣。」
units.en: On his deathbed he said, ‘I need not blush before the ancients—I have lived as long as many of them.’

units.zh: 王遐，字桓子，簡順皇后父，驃騎將軍述之從叔也。
units.en: Wang Xia, courtesy name Huanzi, father of Empress Jianshun, was a collateral paternal uncle of Wang Shu, Grand General Who Gallops as if Flying.

units.zh: 少以華族，仕至光祿勳。
units.en: Born to a great house, he rose to Supervisor of the Household.

units.zh: 甯康初，追贈特進、光祿大夫，加散騎常侍，諡曰靖。
units.en: Early in Ningkang he was posthumously honored as Exalted Marcher and Grand Master of Splendid Carriage with Regular Cavalier Attendant, posthumous name Jing.

units.zh: 長子恪，領軍將軍。
units.en: His eldest son Wang Ke became General Who Commands the Army.

units.zh: 恪子欣之，豫章太守，秩中二千石。
units.en: Wang Ke’s son Wang Xinzhi served as Administrator of Yuzhang at the two-thousand-shi rank.

units.zh: 欣之弟歡之，廣州刺史。
units.en: His brother Wang Huanzhi became Inspector of Guangzhou.

units.zh: 遐少子臻，崇德衛尉。
units.en: Wang Xia’s youngest son Wang Zhen was Commandant of the Guards at Chongde.

units.zh: 王蘊，字叔仁，孝武定皇后父，司徒左長史濛之子也。
units.en: Wang Yun, courtesy name Shuren, father of Empress Xiaowu Ding, was the son of Wang Meng, senior clerk on the minister’s left.

units.zh: 起家佐著作郎，累遷尚書吏部郎。
units.en: He began as assistant editorial director and rose to head of the personnel bureau in the Department of State Affairs.

units.zh: 性平和，不抑寒素，每一官缺，求者十輩，蘊無所是非。
units.en: Even-tempered, he did not slight men of humble origin; when a post opened and dozens applied, he refused to pick favorites in advance.

units.zh: 時簡文帝為會稽王，輔政，蘊輒連狀白之，曰：「某人有地，某人有才。」
units.en: While Emperor Jianwen, then Prince of Kuaiji, was assisting in government, Wang Yun sent him lists: ‘This man has standing; that man has ability.’

units.zh: 務存進達，各隨其方，故不得者無怨焉。
units.en: He pushed every candidate on his merits, so those passed over had no cause for bitterness.

units.zh: 補吳興太守，甚有德政。
units.en: As Administrator of Wuxing he governed with conspicuous virtue.

units.zh: 屬郡荒人饑，輒開倉贍恤。
units.en: When famine struck his jurisdiction, he opened the granaries without waiting for higher approval.

units.zh: 主簿執諫，請先列表上待報，蘊曰：「今百姓嗷然，路有饑饉，若表上須報，何以救將死之命乎！
units.en: His chief clerk urged him to seek permission first. Wang Yun replied, ‘The people are starving in the streets; if we wait on paperwork, we let them die!’

units.zh: 專輒之愆，罪在太守，且行仁義而敗，無所恨也。」
units.en: If acting on my own is a crime, blame the administrator; I would rather fail doing right than watch them perish.’

units.zh: 於是大振貸之，賴蘊全者十七八焉。
units.en: He distributed grain on a large scale; perhaps eight in ten survivors owed their lives to him.

units.zh: 朝廷以違科免蘊官，士庶詣闕訟之，詔特左降晉陵太守。
units.en: The court cashiered him for breaking regulations, but a popular petition at the palace gates won him a reduced sentence: demotion to Administrator of Jinling.

units.zh: 復有惠化，百姓歌之。
units.en: There too his benevolent rule won the people’s songs.

units.zh: 定后立，以后父，遷光祿大夫，領五兵尚書、本州大中正，封建昌縣侯。
units.en: When the Ding empress was enthroned, he became Grand Master of Splendid Carriage, minister of the Five Armies, senior rectifier for his province, and Marquis of Jianchang.

units.zh: 蘊以恩澤賜爵，非三代令典，固辭不受。
units.en: He argued that a title won only through imperial favor was not like the old canonical grants and refused it.

units.zh: 朝廷敦勸，終不肯拜，乃授都督京口諸軍事、左將軍、徐州刺史、假節，復固讓。
units.en: Despite repeated pressure he would not accept the marquisate, so they named him commander at Jingkou, General of the Left, and Inspector of Xuzhou with credentials—which he also tried to refuse.

units.zh: 謝安謂蘊曰：「卿居后父之重，不應妄自菲薄，以虧時遇，宜依褚公故事，但令在貴權於事不事耳。
units.en: Xie An told him, ‘As the empress’s father you must not sell yourself short. Do as Chu Pou did: take the high title but leave day-to-day duties to others.’

units.zh: 蘊以姻戚，不欲在內，苦求外出，復以為都督浙江東五郡、鎮軍將軍、會稽內史，常侍如故。
units.en: Unwilling to remain at court as an in-law, he begged for a provincial assignment and was named commander of the five eastern Zhe commanderies, Army-securing General, and interior secretary of Kuaiji, still holding his cavalier attendant title.

units.zh: 蘊素嗜酒，末年尤甚。
units.en: Wang Yun had always loved wine, and drank more heavily in his last years.

units.zh: 及在會稽，略少醒日，然猶以和簡為百姓所悅。
units.en: In Kuaiji he was seldom sober, yet his easy, unpretentious manner kept the people fond of him.

units.zh: 時王悅來拜墓，蘊子恭往省之，素相善，遂留十餘日方還。
units.en: When Wang Yue came to sweep the family tombs, Wang Yun’s son Wang Gong, an old friend, visited him and stayed more than ten days.

units.zh: 太元九年卒，年五十五，追贈左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司。
units.en: He died in 384 at fifty-five and was posthumously honored as Left Grand Master of Splendid Carriage with Three Dukes’ establishment.

units.zh: 孝武帝崩，王國寶夜欲開門入為遺詔，爽距之，曰：「大行晏駕，皇太子未至，敢入者斬！」
units.en: After Emperor Xiaowu’s death, Wang Guobao tried to force the palace gates at night to forge a will. Wang Shuang blocked him: ‘The emperor has just died and the crown prince is not here—enter and you die!’

units.zh: 爽嘗與會稽王道子飲，道子醉呼爽為小子，爽曰：「亡祖長史與簡文皇帝為布衣之交。
units.en: Once, drinking with Prince Daozi of Kuaiji, the prince drunk called him ‘boy.’ Wang Shuang replied, ‘My late grandfather was sworn friend to Emperor Jianwen when both were commoners.’

units.zh: 弘理儀形外朗，季野神鑒內融，仲祖溫潤風流，幼道清虛寡欲，皆擅名江表，見重當時，豈惟后族之英華，抑亦搢紳之令望者也。
units.en: Du Yi’s looks were open and bright; Chu Pou read men with inward clarity; Wang Meng moved with gentle grace; He Zhun lived spare and detached—all were luminaries south of the Yangzi and pillars of their age, ornaments not only to the imperial in-laws but to the whole gentry.

sourceCorrectionContext.reason: Current reviewed name correction:王叔仁 in s0021 is WangYun 王蘊 (s0230); source-equivalent local records remain separate until normal canonical merge. Review each owned date independently, using the complete relevant primary context.

units.zh: 若褚季野之畏避朝權，王叔仁之固求出鎮，用能全身遠害，有可稱焉。
units.en: Chu Pou feared and avoided the power of the court, and Wang Yun insisted on seeking a command away from court; this enabled them to preserve themselves and avoid harm, and their conduct deserves praise.
units.literal: As for Chu Jiye’s fearing and avoiding court power, and Wang Shuren’s firmly seeking to go out and hold a command, by this they were able to preserve the body and keep far from harm—there is something to praise in that.

units.zh: 王蘊，字叔仁，孝武定皇后父，司徒左長史濛之子也。
units.en: Wang Yun, courtesy name Shuren, father of Empress Xiaowu Ding, was the son of Wang Meng, senior clerk on the minister’s left.
units.literal: Wang Yun, styled Shuren, was the father of Empress Xiaowu Ding and the son of Wang Meng, senior clerk on the minister’s left.

units.zh: 頃之，徵拜尚書左僕射，將軍如故，遷丹陽尹，即本軍號加散騎常侍。
units.en: Soon he was recalled as Left Vice Director while keeping his general’s rank, then made Intendant of Danyang with the added title of Regular Cavalier Attendant.
units.literal: In a short while, he was summoned and appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, general as before, promoted to Intendant of Danyang, on his original army title adding Regular Cavalier Attendant.

units.zh: 蘊以姻戚，不欲在內，苦求外出，復以為都督浙江東五郡、鎮軍將軍、會稽內史，常侍如故。
units.en: Unwilling to remain at court as an in-law, he begged for a provincial assignment and was named commander of the five eastern Zhe commanderies, Army-securing General, and interior secretary of Kuaiji, still holding his cavalier attendant title.
units.literal: Yun, as affinal kin, did not wish to be inside; he bitterly sought to go out; again he was made military overseer of the five commanderies east of the Zhe River, Army-securing General, interior secretary of Kuaiji, Regular Cavalier Attendant as before.

units.zh: 蘊素嗜酒，末年尤甚。
units.en: Wang Yun had always loved wine, and drank more heavily in his last years.
units.literal: Yun by nature was fond of wine; in late years it was especially severe.

units.zh: 及在會稽，略少醒日，然猶以和簡為百姓所悅。
units.en: In Kuaiji he was seldom sober, yet his easy, unpretentious manner kept the people fond of him.
units.literal: When he was in Kuaiji, he had slightly fewer sober days, yet still by mildness and simplicity was pleasing to the hundred surnames.

units.zh: 時王悅來拜墓，蘊子恭往省之，素相善，遂留十餘日方還。
units.en: When Wang Yue came to sweep the family tombs, Wang Yun’s son Wang Gong, an old friend, visited him and stayed more than ten days.
units.literal: At the time Wang Yue came to pay respects at the tomb; Yun’s son Gong went to visit him; they were always on good terms; then he stayed over ten days before returning.

label.en: senior rectifier of his native province
Left Grand Master of Splendid Carriage
opener of office with the honors of the Three Dukes
